newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gehe eyes strong 97 with Lloyds help.
newsitem.headline: Gehe eyes strong 97 with Lloyds help.

text.p: German drugs wholesaler Gehe AG, fresh from winning a long-fought battle for UK drugs group Lloyds Chemists, said on Monday the takeover would help lead to clearly improved 1997 results as the year got off to a strong start.

At a news conference held in Paris, Stuttgart, Germany, based Gehe said it expected sales, including turnover from Lloyds Chemists, to climb by about 10 percent to over 24 billion marks this year from 1996's 21.4 billion marks.

Lloyds Chemists already contributed a significant chunk to Gehe's 13 percent rise in first quarter sales, the group said, adding that without these additional sales, turnover would have risen by only 1.1 percent in the first quarter.

Gehe, Europe's largest drugs wholesaler, also said it expected a "clear improvement" in pre-tax operating profit this year, after first quarter pre-tax profit, excluding Lloyds Chemists, already showed about a five percent increase.
The group plans to raise its pre-tax operating profit to 450 to 500 million marks this year, up from last year's 407 million mark result.
Last year the group more than doubled its net profit to 440 million marks from 211.5 million marks in 1995.

While Gehe management board chairman Dieter Kaemmerer told the news conference that significant synergies would be generated with Lloyds Chemists, he also said he planned to slim down the group by selling off various units.
"We plan to concentrate on the core pharmaceutical wholesale and retail business," Kaemmerer said.
Gehe hopes to bring in about one third of the 685 million sterling it spent to beat out U.K. rival Unichem for Lloyds.
Targeted to go will be Gehe's 404 health food shops Holland & Barrett producing an annual turnover of 91 million sterling.

Gehe also plans to sell its pharmaceutical production eyecare products which post sales of 16 million sterling and the veterinary medicine production, distribution and wholesale businesses with annual sales of 105 million sterling.
"We have decided these units are not part of the core business and talks with prospective buyers are underway," Kaemmerer said.
Besides Lloyds, Gehe also owns some 365 pharmacies belonging to the AAH chain in the U.K. "From today's vantage our investment in the U.K. is very positive," Kaemmerer said.
After the last years' major acquisitions, he said the group would first catch its breath before starting anew on possible takeovers.
"We have no plans for further takeovers in the pipeline," Kaemmerer said, adding the group was watching pharmaceutical market developments very carefully.
